summary: Terry Kleeman is a sinologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of British Columbia (~1980–1988). He became a professor at the University of Colorado Boulder around 1998 and taught Thomas J. Mazanec.

Terton Sogyal was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied under numerous teachers including Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Pema Vajra 01, and Patrul Rinpoche, and taught figures including the 13th Dalai Lama and Dongak Chokyi Gyatso.

Teruji Ishizu was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1923–1926). He held posts at Tohoku University, serving as president (1963–1966), and later served as professor at Keio and Komazawa Universities (1966).

Tessa Bartholomeusz was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. Educated at the University of Florida, Florida State University, and the University of Virginia, she taught at IUPUI (~1991–2001) and was Professor of Religion at Florida State University (1993).
Tessa Verney Wheeler was a scholar in the field of history and archaeology. She was educated at Addey and Stanhope School from 1905 to 1911 and studied at University College London from 1911 to 1914.

Tetsuei Sato was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1925–1931). He served as a professor at Taisho University and Gifu Kyoritsu University (~1967–1973), and became an emeritus professor at Ryukoku University (~1968–1989).
Tetsuhiko Shibata is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University under teachers Eijun Hattori, Yukan Ozawa, and Mitsuo Sato.

Tetsujiro Inoue was a philosopher and religious studies scholar who studied at Tokyo, Heidelberg, Leipzig, and Berlin. He served as professor and dean at the University of Tokyo, professor at Toyo University, and president of Daito Bunka University (1925).

Tetsuo Otani is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda and Komazawa Universities. He held multiple leadership roles at Komazawa University, including president (2002–2006), and later served as president of Tohoku Fukushi University (2015–2019).

Tetsuo Yamaori is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University (~1950–1954). He held posts at Tohoku University, the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (~1988–2001), and Kyoto University of the Arts (~2005–2009).

Tetsuro Noguchi was a scholar of sinology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. Over his career, he held academic posts at Yokohama National University (~1968–1978), the University of Tsukuba (~1978–1996), and J. F. Oberlin University (~1996–2003).

Tetsuro Watsuji was a philosophy and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and under Natsume Sōseki and Martin Heidegger. He held chairs in ethics at Kyoto University (1925–1949) and the University of Tokyo (1934–1949).

Tetsuzo Tanikawa was a philosopher and Japanologist who studied at Kyoto University (~1916–1919). His academic career included posts at Doshisha University (~1924–1928) and as a professor at Hosei University (~1938–1965).
Teun Goudriaan is an Indology scholar who served at Utrecht University, where his presence is attested in 1989 and as Professor Emeritus in 2000.
Thanon Chitkament is a scholar in history and archaeology who studied under the guidance of Vishwas D. Gogte and co-guide P. S. Joshi (attested 2021).

Theodoor Paul Galestin was an Indology and archaeology scholar who studied under Nicolaas Johannes Krom (~1931–1936). In 1957, he became a professor of South and Southeast Asian archaeology and ancient history at Leiden University, where he taught Jan Fontein.

Theodor Aufrecht was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1843–1847). He served as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Edinburgh (1861–1875) and as Professor at the University of Bonn (1875–1889).

Theodor Benfey was an Indologist and linguist who completed his education, Ph.D., and Habilitation at the University of Göttingen. He served there as Privatdozent (1834) and Ordinarius professor (1862–1881), teaching numerous notable scholars.
Theodor Bloch was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Leipzig under Ernst Windisch (~1888–1892) and continued his studies under Georg Bühler (~1892–1894).

Theodor Goldstücker was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Königsberg, Bonn, and under Eugène Burnouf and Christian Lassen. He was appointed Professor of Sanskrit at the University of London and University College London from 1851 until 1872.
